clue.text: Check Murphy is coming back

indicators.note: coming back tells us the word for a Murphy is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a murphy is slang for a potato, which is a tuber

explanation.surface: Someone named Murphy is returning to keep things in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns TUBER round to give the answer. A murphy is old slang (originally Irish) for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to check or repel it with a counter-argument.

clue.text: Kind of course fee

explanation.surface: A note about what sort of charge a course carries.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law a refresher is the extra daily fee paid to a barrister when a case runs beyond its first day.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher course updates old skills; a refresher is also a barrister's further payment for a continuing trial.

clue.text: Less draped about in silks

indicators.note: in places the word for about within the letters standing for silks

parts.note: senior barristers are called silks, and together barristers form the Bar
re is a short word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone in silk garments is wearing fewer covering layers.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a King's or Queen's Counsel, a senior British barrister, so silks together stand for the Bar; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barer has less covering, being more naked or less clothed than another.

clue.text: Tempting, but it can bite a few people

parts.note: a tooth is the thing in the mouth that bites
some means a few people, as in 'some say'

explanation.surface: Something looks appetising, yet it might snap at a handful of folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is delicious and appetising, hence tempting to eat.

clue.text: Book cover has to repeat the title

parts.note: to copy is to repeat or reproduce
a title in law is a right to own something

explanation.surface: A book jacket must reprint the book's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book cover' suggests a dust jacket, but it is the legal protection that covers a book's text.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal protection that shields an author's published work from being reproduced.

clue.text: High passage makes jazz freak move his feet

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
to walk is to move one's feet

explanation.surface: A raised walkway sets a jazz fan stepping about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A catwalk is a narrow raised walkway, such as a fashion runway or a gangway high above a stage.

clue.text: Criticise a guerilla's swagger

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
Che Guevara was the famous Argentine guerilla leader

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a rebel fighter's arrogant strut.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence of style, a dashing swagger.

clue.text: Sound examples of it are D and X, both ending in C

definitions.text: Sound examples of it are D and X, both ending in C

parts.words: Sound examples of it are D and X, both ending in C
parts.note: the letters D and X sound like the Dee and the Exe, and C sounds like sea, where both of those waterways finish

explanation.surface: A puzzle about letters: D and X, each finished off with a C.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'D' and 'X' aloud as Dee and Exe, two British flowing waters, and 'C' as sea, where each ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dee and the Exe are British waterways that flow into the sea.

clue.text: Everyone in support of high level operation shows courage

indicators.note: in places the word for everyone within the word for the overhead frame

parts.note: a gantry is an overhead frame supporting cranes or signals working at height
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody backing a top-level mission displays bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'shows' is a link word joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is bravery, especially in battle, so it means courage.

clue.text: Bird perched on an enormous man

indicators.note: in a down answer, perched on puts the bird's letters above the next piece

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird sits on a giant of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'perched on' puts TIT above AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of colossal size or strength, after the giants of Greek myth.

clue.text: Abandoned grotto crumbling into the marsh

indicators.note: into places the scrambled letters within the word for the marsh

parts.note: a fen is a low marshy area, as in the English Fens

indicators.note: crumbling means the letters of grotto fall apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deserted cave is falling apart into a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' gives ORGOTT, and 'into' signals that it goes in the fen; England's Fens are marshy lowlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been left behind and neglected, so abandoned.

clue.text: Get state permit to have a servant

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Someone seeks official permission to employ a domestic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get', 'to have a' are link words around the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a manservant who looks after his employer's clothes and personal needs.

clue.text: Huge cost of electrical safety precaution

explanation.surface: A remark on the expense of protecting against shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'cost the earth' is to cost a great deal; the earth wire is the British name for what Americans call a ground wire.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'costs the earth' means is very expensive; an earth wire grounds an appliance against shocks.

clue.text: So sure to make a discovery

parts.note: as can mean so, as in 'as good'
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Being so confident leads to finding something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, establishing a fact.

clue.text: Ate basin of sea-food

parts.note: had means ate, as in 'had lunch'
a dock is an enclosed basin of water for ships

explanation.surface: Someone ate a bowl of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basin' looks like a bowl, but here is a harbour basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Haddock is a North Atlantic fish widely eaten, so an example of seafood.

clue.text: Decide to set boy up with the trappings of rank

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the boy's name is written going upwards

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
ermine is the white fur worn on robes of peers and judges as a mark of rank

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to set a lad up with the outward signs of status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TED to DET. Ermine trims the ceremonial robes of British peers.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve something, so to decide.

clue.text: Big cars on the US Atlantic seaboard?

parts.note: the Atlantic seaboard of America is its east, abbreviated E
the States is a name for the US

explanation.surface: Large vehicles cruising along America's east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Eastern states lie on the Atlantic coast. An estate car is the British term for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large cars with a long rear load space, known in America as station wagons.

clue.text: Get great help working the scoreboard

indicators.note: working means the letters of great help are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Get plenty of assistance operating the scores display.
explanation.walkthrough: A telegraph is a cricket scoreboard showing the score in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a telegraph board is a simple scoreboard displaying the score to spectators.

clue.text: Secondary activities include minor verse

parts.note: side means minor, as in a side issue
lines of verse are poetry

explanation.surface: Extra pursuits may involve some light poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidelines are activities pursued alongside one's main job, so secondary ones.

clue.text: Go back to buy another round

explanation.surface: Leaving the bar or getting more drinks in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as RE-TREAT: treat everyone again.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw; to re-treat friends is to stand them drinks again.

clue.text: Blandishments well described by Dormouse

explanation.surface: Flattery is the sort of thing a sleepy storyteller recounts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters who lived at the bottom of a syrup well.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet cloying flattery is called syrupy talk; and the Dormouse's tale in Alice features a well of syrup.

clue.text: Inconvenienced by action to suppress poem

indicators.note: to suppress here means the deed holds down and encloses the poem

parts.note: a deed is an action
a lay is a narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: Someone is put out by a move to ban some verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suppress' signals the container, the deed holding the poem down; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held up is a hindrance, so delayed people are put out or inconvenienced.

clue.text: Due to eat second course

indicators.note: to eat means the word for due swallows the letter for second

parts.note: a desert, as in 'just deserts', is what someone is due

explanation.surface: It is time to have the next course of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts S inside DESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert is the sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Lack of energy deters sin that is fashionable

indicators.note: fashionable read as made into a new fashion signals that deters sin is rearranged

explanation.surface: Fatigue puts people off the sin that is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges DETERS SIN; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness is weariness, the condition of having no energy left.

clue.text: It's forbidden to put a native inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for a native within the little word to

parts.note: Abo is a dated and offensive Australian slang word for an Aboriginal person

explanation.surface: Housing a local person is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' signals the container; 'It's' and 'put' are link words. The native term is dated, offensive Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo thing is prohibited by custom, so forbidden.

clue.text: Repudiate saint — he's French

parts.note: to deny is to repudiate

explanation.surface: Disown the holy man, since he comes from France.
explanation.walkthrough: St Denys is the patron saint of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Denys is a man's name in French, borne by France's patron saint.

clue.text: King to weaken, until Parsifal wins this?

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
to ail is to be sickly or weaken

explanation.surface: A king fades away while a knight triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: Parsifal is the knight of Wagner's opera who wins the holy vessel; 'to' and 'until' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the holy vessel is the prize of the knight Parsifal's quest.

clue.text: Advanced to a crisis

parts.note: a head is a crisis point, as in 'come to a head'

explanation.surface: Things progressed until they reached breaking point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being further forward than others, someone advanced is in front.

clue.text: Put one in store — a wee one

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one within the word for store

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing produce
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Storing something, a small person is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside BARN. Bairn is Scottish for a child, and 'wee' is Scottish for small; 'Put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bairn is a young child in Scots and northern English dialect.

clue.text: One way to be delivered from the emperor

explanation.surface: A method of being rescued from a tyrant ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' looks like rescued but means born; the surgical birth was traditionally linked to Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caesarean section is a surgical birth; the adjective also means belonging to Caesar.

clue.text: Take spare writing implement, in a way, out of pocket

parts.note: over means spare, as in left over

indicators.note: in places the writing tool within the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: Grab a spare pen, somehow, from your pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'Take' is a link. 'pocket' suggests a place, but 'out of pocket' means having lost money.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has spent too much is left short of money, out of pocket.

clue.text: Where one would find a wandering shade?

definitions.text: Where one would find a wandering shade?

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of shade stray into a different order

explanation.surface: Asking where a roaming ghost might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges SHADE; a shade is also a ghost, so the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the underworld is where the ghosts of the dead roam.
